Rugix SECURITY.md: only the latest minor version branch receives security updates; reports go to Silitics
Rugix Ctrl does not mark boot groups good or bad automatically; its default grub/uboot/systemd-boot flows have no dead man's switch and a committed system is assumed to stay good

Rugix two-stage update: an uncommitted trial system falls back on the next reboot; `rugix-ctrl system commit` must run from the booted new system; the core/rugix-auto-commit recipe commits whatever system boots, including an old one after a rollback
A failing Rugix system-commit/pre-commit hook prevents the commit

Rugix requires every bundle to be verified by an embedded CMS signature against a configured root or by --bundle-hash; it currently supports CMS signatures with a single signer only; HSM signing is possible via external openssl cms

No certificate revocation (CRL), signer revocation or anti-downgrade feature is documented in Rugix Ctrl 1.4 docs (grep for revoc/CRL/expir/downgrade returned no matches); Umbrel implements revocation and anti-downgrade in its own daemon [status note: absence in docs at pinned SHA]

Rugix power-loss semantics: power loss before the durability boundary leaves only the inactive target partially written and not selected for boot; reinstalling overwrites it; after boot selection the boot flow's trial/rollback applies [status note: doc; lab pending]

Rugix boot flows: uboot, grub, systemd-boot, rauc-uboot, rauc-grub, mender-uboot, mender-grub, rpi-uboot, rpi-tryboot (Pi 4 and newer), custom; RAUC/Mender-compatible flows allow in-field migration from those tools
Rugix grub flow keeps primary and secondary copies of the boot-partition variable with SHA1 files so GRUB can fall back if one copy is corrupted by power loss
No Jetson/Tegra/L4T integration exists in rugix/rugix, rugix/rugix-bsps (boards: NXP i.MX, Rockchip), rugix/meta-rugix or rugix/rugix-docs at the pinned SHAs (grep absence) [status note: absence]
Rugix bootstrapping can create or grow the partition layout on first boot; the layout is defined in system configuration and applied during bootstrapping

Silitics GmbH maintains Rugix; its site lists Umbrel, Enmo, eChecker and Aqa Technologies as users and claims Rugix powers tens of thousands of devices (vendor claim) [status note: vendor claim; not independently verified; the claim is worded as that party's statement]
